A sharp clang echoed through the dimly lit workshop as Calla dropped the wrench, its metallic body bouncing once before settling among the scattered tools on the concrete floor. She took a moment to catch her breath, wiping the sweat from her brow with the back of her hand. The air was thick with the smell of oil and metal, a familiar scent that clung to her skin and filled her lungs, grounding her in this chaotic sanctuary.

Outside, the world pulsed with the life of the city, the distant hum of traffic mingling with the occasional shout from a street vendor. But in here, time felt suspended, the outside noise fading into a muted background. Calla leaned against the workbench, its surface littered with half-finished projects and crumpled sketches, her fingers tracing the edges of a rusted gear. Each groove told a story of wear and tear, much like her own life.

She glanced at the clock on the wall, its hands ticking relentlessly forward, but she wasn’t ready to leave yet. Not when she could still taste the salt of her own determination, the way it lingered on her lips like a promise. The weight of her father’s expectations hung heavy in the air, a specter that loomed over her every decision. She could almost hear his voice, echoing in her mind, reminding her of the legacy she was meant to uphold, the family name she was supposed to honor.

“Calla?” The voice pulled her from her reverie, warm and familiar. It was Finn, his presence like a gentle breeze that stirred the stale air. He stepped into the workshop, brushing dust off his worn leather jacket, his dark hair tousled and wild. “You still at it?”

“Just trying to finish this before the sun sets,” she replied, forcing a smile that felt more like a mask than a reflection of her mood. She turned back to the workbench, grabbing the wrench again, but her focus was slipping. “What about you? Shouldn’t you be on your way to that meeting?”

Finn shrugged, his eyes sparkling with mischief. “They can wait. I’d rather be here, watching you wrestle with your mechanical monsters.” He leaned against the doorframe, arms crossed, a lazy smile playing on his lips. “Besides, they don’t know what they’re missing.”

Calla laughed, the sound surprising her. It felt good, lightening the tension that had knotted in her stomach. “You really think I’m wrestling?” She raised an eyebrow, the corners of her mouth twitching. “More like a stubborn mule refusing to budge.”

“More like a fierce warrior,” Finn countered, stepping closer, the warmth of his presence wrapping around her like a cozy blanket. “You’ve got this, Calla. I’ve seen you work miracles with less.”

She met his gaze, the sincerity in his green eyes igniting a flicker of hope within her. It was easy to forget her doubts when he was around, his belief in her like a shield against the world’s skepticism. “Miracles? I’m just trying to make something that doesn’t fall apart after one use.”

“Even the smallest inventions can change lives,” he said, his voice low and earnest. “You know that better than anyone. Just look at what your mom did with that old generator.”
